messages:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created — Ferris (dedicated pool: ferris-prod) reported GPU node node-17 kernel ECC spike; automatic drain started. Pager target: oncall-sre.

oncall-sre: Got the page, looking now. any immediate customer-impact flags?

alex-m: I see terraform-managed node in pool is in "DRAINING" and a few tenants reported increased retries. No 5xx observed from API, but latency climbs on long-gen routes.

tae-s: Which customers are on ferris-prod reserved? We should notify account teams.

sam-cs: Ferris is used by Ferris Health (enterprise VPC). I just pinged AM and they want status for active sessions. Customer impact: inference requests are being handed off to fallback nodes, a handful of long requests timed out and retried.

marie-sre: tl;dr: node-17 ECC errors -> kernel reported AER/AER corrected errors -> nvml reset attempted -> driver NIC reset -> node marked for replace. We're in auto-drain path but need manual evict for stateful tenants.

opslead: Tagging devops-hw to coordinate hardware replacement scheduling and check if this is noisy (multiple nodes) or isolated.

devops-hw: On it — grabbing logs, also running bmc power cycle to see if ECC persists. If hardware flaps, we'll plan hotswap during maintenance window but need immediate mitigations.

oncall-sre: Mitigation plan: 1) Ensure tenant isolation for Ferris Health VPC by pinning their serving to reserved fallback pool ferris-fallback. 2) Increase redundancy of routing so in-flight requests drain gracefully (kv-cache TTL extend). 3) Notify AM/CS with ETA. Anyone object?

alex-m: I can change routing policy for ferris-prod -> ferris-fallback for that customer only. Will do a canary first for 10% traffic then ramp.

tae-s: Please hold off channel-wide rollout — do per-tenant mapping only. We have some other tenants that rely on NVLink infers.

marie-sre: Command I'm running now (will paste logs):
```
# check nvml errors
/journalctl -k -u nvidia-persistenced | tail -n 50
# drain command
redwoodctl node drain node-17 --force --reason "ECC spike auto-drain"
```

oncall-sre: Results: nvml shows 37 corrected ECC errors in last 20m. drain command returned success. Node eviction started, active sessions flagged for handoff.

sam-cs: I told Ferris Health: "We're actively draining a GPU node in your dedicated pool. We're routing traffic to a fallback pool and expect minimal interruption for new requests. We'll follow up with postmortem and mitigation steps." They asked for estimated time to restore full capacity.

devops-hw: BMC power cycle cleared transient faults but nvml still reports intermittent ECC increments. I'm ordering replacement GPU board; ETA 6 hours. If replacement can't be done faster, we'll leave node cordoned.

opslead: For immediate capacity, can we burst to shared spare-hosts? What's the cost/tenant isolation impact?

alex-m: We can temporarily enable burst to shared-spare but need to mask telemetry and ensure Ferris Health data doesn't leave VPC — routing supports edge-level isolation, but I'd prefer ferris-fallback (reserved) to avoid any compliance issues.

marie-sre: SRE playbook tasks completed: node cordoned, active pods migrated where possible, canaries moved. Monitoring: token-level latency up ~12% for affected tenant during handoff window. No 500 spikes.

oncall-sre: Assigning follow-ups: devops-hw to coordinate hardware replace (ticket HW-7891), alex-m to complete tenant-only routing change and ramp, sam-cs to keep customer looped, opslead to decide on burst policy if more nodes degrade.

sam-cs: I'll send a short update to Ferris Health with ETA for capacity restoration (~6h) and note the handoff mitigations. Will ask if they want a phone bridge.

opslead: If ECC rate increases beyond threshold, we'll trigger cross-tenant fallback and open a broader incident. Keep me updated every 30m.

oncall-sre: A few actionables now:
- alex-m: apply per-tenant routing rule (10m) -> confirm
- devops-hw: confirm replacement ETA in ticket (15m) -> confirm
- sam-cs: customer update sent (20m) -> confirm
- marie-sre: watch for error regression and post logs to thread (ongoing)

alex-m: Routing change applied for Ferris Health -> ferris-fallback (10% canary). Observing request distribution now.

devops-hw: HW ticket updated: replacement scheduled in 5.5h, expedited pickup requested. Marked node as DO NOT SCALE.

marie-sre: Monitoring note: after routing change, retries reduced, latency settling. I'll post a 30m update.

sam-cs: Update sent to Ferris Health: confirmed handoff and 6h ETA for full restore. They asked to be informed when node is returned to pool.

opslead: Good. If anything spikes or customer impact widens, escalate to incident commander. For now continue with handoff cadence.

inc-bot: Incident status changed: INVESTIGATING -> MITIGATED_FOR_CUSTOMER (fallback routing effective).

oncall-sre: Closing loop for now. Will reopen if ECC counters climb or further nodes show similar pattern. Postmortem assigned to marie-sre + devops-hw + alex-m.

marie-sre: I'll collect kernel logs, nvml output, and routing diffs and drop in the postmortem doc after incident stabilizes.

sam-cs: Customer acknowledged and appreciated quick mitigation. They want a follow-up call tomorrow.

opslead: Thanks team. Leaving thread open for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:
